reason: loadRoutingTable is an async fs operation. Making the function async is the minimal change; all call sites in app.mjs gained await. The alternative (sync fs.readFileSync) would contradict the codebase's async-first IO pattern.

decision: Routing table is advisory — never auto-overrides options.model
reason: Auto-switching models based on bench scores would surprise users mid-session and break deterministic replay. Exposing the table in options.routingTable lets future surfaces (TUI /model auto) activate it explicitly.

decision: cheapModel falls back to editModel when no other model clears threshold
reason: Single-model setups (the common local case) must produce a valid routing table. Using editModel for cheap tasks costs a little latency but keeps the table always usable.

decision: buildCausalStory is a pure function — all I/O in loadRunAnalysis, story-building takes data only
reason: Pure functions are trivially testable without temp files or mocks. The 10 story-builder tests create no disk fixtures. The same separation also lets server and CLI renderers share one builder without duplicating I/O logic.

decision: HTML renderer is self-contained — inline CSS, no external assets
reason: The page must be usable offline and serveable as a single HTTP response. External CDN fonts or stylesheets would break air-gapped local use and add a network dependency to a tool that is explicitly local-first.

decision: /why in TUI uses dynamic import for forensics module
reason: The TUI module is already large. A static import would add forensics.mjs to the startup parse cost on every TUI launch, even for users who never call /why. Dynamic import is cached by Node after the first call, so repeated use has no overhead penalty.

decision: Server why routes require a recorded runDir — 404 otherwise
reason: The server tracks run directories only after a run finishes (result.runDir written into state.runDirs). Returning 404 with a clear message is safer than attempting to guess or reconstruct the path from the run ID while a run is active.

decision: fs.watch with recursive:true instead of chokidar
reason: Node.js 24 supports recursive directory watching natively. Adding chokidar would violate the no-new-dependencies rule and undermine the local-first, zero-install goal. The native API is adequate for watching a single project directory.

decision: dryRun:true enforced in watch loop — repairs are always pending reviews
reason: Auto-applying model-proposed repairs in the background would be unsafe. The phase 98 apply gate already provides the right review mechanic. The watch loop reuses it by always setting dryRun:true and never passing yes:true.

decision: No-progress guard caps repair attempts at 3 per file-change cycle
reason: Without a cap the loop could spin and consume local model capacity indefinitely if the model repeatedly proposes repairs that the user ignores. Three attempts gives the user enough signal before the loop backs off.

decision: packages/repomap/ is a copy of src/repomap/, not a workspace symlink or monorepo dependency
reason: Keeping the package as an independent directory with copied files avoids npm workspaces complexity (Node 24 workspaces have hoisting edge cases) and keeps the publication path simple. The sync obligation is documented in the phase file and in the package README.

decision: engines: node>=22 in @kodr/repomap package.json, not node>=24
reason: The library uses only node:fs/promises, node:path, node:crypto, and node:os — all available in Node 22. Requiring 24 would unnecessarily narrow the audience. The main kodr CLI requires 24 because it uses later Node features; the library does not.

decision: Fix post-write-sensor.mjs to import classifyLanguage through src/repomap/index.mjs
reason: The boundary test was already enforcing this rule and was failing with a violation introduced in an earlier phase. Phase 108's publication work made the violation visible. Fixed in the same commit to keep the boundary clean before the package ships.

decision: Tool loop short-circuits exact repeat tool calls and forces a final no-tools turn instead of throwing on budget exhaustion
reason: Dogfooding showed the model burning all 8 turns re-running the same failing test after its write attempts were blocked. Nothing in this loop can change between identical calls (there is no write tool and allowlisted commands are read-only test runs), so repeats are pure waste, and converting exhaustion into a forced final proposal turn preserves the model's correct diagnosis instead of discarding it.

decision: Budget exhaustion in completeWithToolCalls salvages the conversation instead of propagating LoopBudgetError
reason: The hard-throw path discarded all turns of conversation and usage, which directly caused a wrong root-cause diagnosis from the artifacts. A harness that loses its evidence on the failure path gets its failures explained wrong.

decision: Keep repair-timeout strategy, wrong-path apply gating, and qwen3.6 nativeToolCalls default as open questions in NEXT.md
reason: Each is a design tradeoff rather than a clear bug; fixing them without more dogfooding evidence risks tuning to a single model and two test runs.

decision: D5 verdict: KEEP healing
reason: After three root-cause fixes the heal loop works end-to-end on the real local model: heal trial 5 healed the planted bug in one 4.8s repair turn (kodr-testing/phase-110/heal-trial-5, run 2026-06-12T05-00-49.394Z, kodr why fully green including Healing ok). The feature was not conceptually broken — it was starved (no imported sources in context), poisoned (json_schema on a reasoning model), and blindfolded (wrong-path heuristic skipping verification). Each fix is small and evidence-backed.

decision: Verification is ground truth in the heal loop; path heuristics may steer but never gate
reason: Trial 4 proved a 'wrong-path' write can be the correct fix and that any heuristic preventing or skipping measurement makes the loop blind to its own success. The D3 pre-apply rejection gate was removed in the same phase that introduced it; wrong-path remains as post-verification steering (warn once, exhaust on repeat).

decision: Repair turns never send response_format
reason: A/B on the identical stalled repair prompt: 6s correct fix without json_schema vs empty content/240s+ stalls with it on qwen3.6 via LM Studio. Reasoning-model profiles may want this more broadly; left to a future phase to generalize.

decision: The model response is evidence, not a single parse target — extract and merge all valid proposal envelopes
reason: gemma-4's multi-block narration pattern and qwen3.6's multi-pass implementation both produce multiple proposal-shaped JSON blocks in one response. Discarding all but the first (or last) silently loses real file content. The merge contract — last-wins per path for files, concatenation for patches/messages/status/scratchpad from last envelope — recovers all substantive content without regressing single-envelope responses.

decision: Empty-final-turn nudge is opt-in via options.nudgeEmptyTurn and fires only on whitespace-only content (0 non-whitespace chars)
reason: Setting nudgeEmptyTurn globally broke all existing tests that return short text answers (e.g. 'ok', 'Done.', 'First answer.'). The production failure mode (qwen3.6 emitting '\n\n' or '  ') has 0 non-whitespace chars, so the threshold is set to exactly 0 non-whitespace. Opt-in via flag means existing paths are unaffected; only agents that must return a JSON proposal envelope (implementer, file-author, standard run) enable it.

decision: Constraint mode is a measured per-model profile capability applied uniformly to every turn type; local measured default is none
reason: A/B measurement (phase-112/ab-structured-output/) confirmed: json_schema stalls both qwen3.6 (phase 110) and gemma-4 (phase 112) on LM Studio >300s. json_object returns HTTP 400 from LM Studio. Unconstrained (none) works for both models in 22s. The correct approach is to measure per model and encode the result as a profile field (structuredOutput), not to guess from provider+tools at request time.

decision: S4 no-proposal steer fires only when responseFormatForRequest returns non-null (mode != none)
reason: S4 should only steer when the model was actually sent a response_format constraint and still returned prose. For local mode='none', the model was never told to return JSON, so prose is a valid response. Gating on responseFormatForRequest({}, options) != null correctly excludes local runs where structuredOutputMode is 'none'.

decision: createChatCompletion always streams on the wire; options.stream is display-only
reason: LM Studio non-streaming hangs indefinitely on some model+request combinations (root-caused in dogfood rounds 2-3). The SSE parser was already complete and requests include_usage. The only escape hatch is --wire-no-stream for debugging servers that cannot stream. This is never chosen automatically.

decision: First-token deadline measured from request start, not first read; empty zero-byte chunks from header-only flushes do not count as first token
reason: Node.js Node.js Readable.toWeb can emit zero-length chunks when the server flushes headers without body data. Counting these as first-token would suppress the deadline incorrectly. The fix: only set firstChunkSeen when value.length > 0 or done=true. The deadline is stored as an absolute timestamp to survive loop iterations without drift.

decision: fake-model-server auto-converts JSON chat responses to SSE when request body includes stream:true
reason: Phase 113 changed the wire to always stream, which would break all 65+ existing tests using the fake server with plain JSON responses. Auto-conversion in the fake server lets existing tests work transparently without requiring each to supply explicit SSE bodies. Tests that supply explicit SSE responses (content-type: text/event-stream) are served as-is.

decision: Tool sentence removed from base contract; moved to a standalone # Tools section rendered only when toolsMode:true
reason: The run-on tool sentence appeared in every system prompt including no-tools mode where there are no tools to call. Separating it into renderToolsBlock() allows clean tools-mode-only inclusion and makes the sentence individually readable. Both renderEditFormatContract (edit-formats.mjs) and renderKodrBaseContract (context-packer.mjs) were updated together to preserve byte-identity.

decision: Environment facts captured once per runPrompt call and passed as environmentFacts to buildWorkspaceContext
reason: Environment facts (cwd, git branch, model id, date) are session-stable within a run. Capturing them once and passing them through guarantees the # Environment block is byte-stable across all context builds in a single run, which preserves prompt-prefix cache hits (phase 87). Each call to captureEnvironmentFacts() makes a git rev-parse check, so a single call is also cheaper.

decision: behaviours and tools sections go into the stable prompt section; environment goes into its own section
reason: Behaviours and tools text is constant (never changes between runs), so it belongs in the most-stable slot alongside the envelope contract. Environment text changes per session (different cwd, model, date) so it gets its own section that is hashed and tracked separately in prompt-prefix.json.

decision: Structural decode-artifact rules applied in repair path only — gate is per-candidate parse failure (blanket-rules-only attempt) OR full-text structural pre-pass when brace-walking fails to produce any candidate
reason: Array-boundary corruption (gpt-oss R2 pattern) can break braceWalkFrom entirely, producing zero candidates from the corrupt text. The repair-path gate cannot operate per-candidate when there are no candidates. Two-pass approach: candidate-level structural repair for cases where blanket-only fails (R1 gemma case); full-text structural pre-pass with re-enumeration for cases where corruption prevents brace-walking (R2 gpt-oss case). Valid-JSON false-positive risk: structural rules only run after a parse failure, so text that parses cleanly without them is never mutated.

decision: R2a replacement uses '},$1' to preserve the captured { rather than adding an extra " before {
reason: Pattern /\},"(\{)/gu captures { in group 1. Replacement '},{\'  would yield },{\'{ (extra {). Correct: },$1 yields },{ since group 1 is {. The " that follows is already in the original text as the start of the key string.
